finding.claim: wipe() never enforces the OWNER role: requireRole() returns a boolean and its result is discarded, so any caller can wipe any tenant.
finding.source: Caller-supplied User record (roles set) and tenant path parameter, POST /tenants/{t}/wipe per comment at line 24. Attacker is any user with no OWNER role; authentication is assumed upstream and not visible in this file.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27, an irreversible tenant-wide destructive operation.

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) is entered with any user u.
requireRole(u, "OWNER") is called and its boolean return value is discarded.
requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role) and does not throw (documented at line 13).
repo.wipe(tenant) executes regardless of whether the role check passed.

finding.guards_checked: requireRole at line 14 returns a boolean and does not throw, so the caller must act on the result; wipe() does not. The sibling export() at src/Admin.java:32 uses checkRole (lines 18-22), which throws, and is correctly enforced. Upstream authentication middleware is not present in the directory, so it could not be verified.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns a boolean and does not throw, and its result is discarded as a bare statement at src/Admin.java:26, so repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs for any user. The sibling export() at lines 31-33 uses checkRole (lines 18-22), which throws, and is enforced. No upstream authorization middleware exists in the repo (only src/Admin.java is present), so none could be verified.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: the boolean from requireRole at src/Admin.java:26 is discarded, so the irreversible repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 runs for any caller, while export() at line 32 correctly uses the throwing checkRole. The attacker needs only to reach wipe(), which requires no OWNER role; the one caveat is that an upstream router could restrict the endpoint to OWNERs, but that code is not in the directory.

finding.claim: wipe() and export() do not verify that the caller belongs to the target tenant; OWNER appears to be a global role, enabling cross-tenant access.
finding.source: Caller's roles set (User record, line 4) and tenant path parameter. Precondition: a user holding OWNER in one tenant can target another tenant.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 and repo.export(tenant) at src/Admin.java:33.

trace.note: User record has only name and roles; no tenant or membership field.
wipe() takes the tenant from the caller without comparing it to any user attribute.
export() has the same gap: the tenant parameter is not checked against the caller.

finding.guards_checked: Role checks at src/Admin.java:26 and :32 test only the role name, not the tenant. This finding depends on roles being global; if they are scoped per tenant upstream, it does not apply. Lower confidence than ADMIN-1.

verdict.guard_found: src/Admin.java:14-16 requireRole returns a bool; its result is discarded at line 26, so it blocks nothing. src/Admin.java:18-22 checkRole throws on a missing role and guards export() at line 32, but it tests only the role name, not the tenant. No tenant-membership check exists anywhere in the file.
verdict.reason: The User record (src/Admin.java:4) carries only name and roles with no tenant, so the OWNER check at line 32 cannot be tenant-scoped, and wipe() at lines 26-27 has no effective check at all because requireRole's bool is discarded. Any caller can therefore pass an arbitrary tenant to repo.wipe (line 27), and an OWNER in any tenant can pass an arbitrary tenant to repo.export (line 33). The one caveat is that per-tenant role scoping upstream, outside this single file, would refute the cross-tenant framing, but the only code available treats roles as a flat set. The candidate's guards_checked also missed that line 26 ignores its result, which makes wipe() worse than described.
